assumptions: Every hypothesis names its test and direction before any test runs.
e-values from tests that read different sources are independent; evidence that read one source is averaged, not multiplied.
limits: A supported hypothesis still needs the literature query it carries before it may be called new.
Bayesian surprise orders follow-ups and never changes a verdict.
bio.jane/contract.question: Which pre-registered hypotheses does a program of falsification tests support, with the false discovery rate controlled across all of them?

description: Run a discovery program end to end under pre-registration: every hypothesis names its test (discover_site_avoidance: a site, optionally a record, and its null; discover_codon_outliers: a gene and its genetic code; validate_gene_trait: a human gene, the trait's own gene or tissues, and GWAS Catalog categories; discover_flag_rates: a cryptic-element flag, optionally a record, against k-let shuffles; discover_tree_incongruence: a locus of a multi-locus alignment, by the ILD test; discover_gene_tree_discordance: a gene alignment against a species tree, by the SH test; discover_reference_stability: a candidate reference gene against its GTEx abundance peers; discover_annotation_contradictions: a UniProt signal peptide or transmembrane segment against the experimentally confirmed ones; discover_reference_concordance: a Cq table whose conditions should rank its reference genes alike; differential_expression: a gene of a DESeq2 fit, up or down in the contrast; gene_set_overrepresentation: a gene set holding more of a gene list than chance; gene_set_enrichment: a gene set toward the top or bottom of a ranked list by GSEA) and direction, and all are registered in a hypothesis ledger before any test runs. Each registered test then runs once over the corpus, every answering result is attached as a κ-calibrated e-value (evidence from another test, a changed parameter or the same data twice is refused and reported), and e-BH decides over all hypotheses, those without evidence included. Returns the verdicts, the whole ledger as a file that imports into Discovery Expert, every run's input, the refusals, and the literature query each supported hypothesis needs before it may be called new. Pass a previous ledger with posterior beliefs to get the follow-up order by Bayesian surprise, which ranks what to test next and never changes a verdict. Also returns the whole program as a sealed run file (every corpus input pinned by SHA-256, the last attempt at each hypothesis); pass it back as `run` to add hypotheses and retry the ones whose test failed, or to research_run_status and resume_research_run. Evidence that read one source (one table, or one sequence under two names) is averaged, not multiplied, and each verdict names the rule.

_files.description: The project: record references shaped like _subject. Their records become library documents a tool names in sequences/parts/document; a trace or alignment is found by file name.

_subject.description: The record to act on: exactly one of sequence, accession (+source), sample (an id from list_samples) or file ({name, text} or {name, base64}); record_index picks one record of several.

alpha.description: e-BH level the verdicts are decided at, across every hypothesis in the ledger.

budget_seconds.description: seconds this call may spend running tests: whole tests run until the budget is spent and the rest are deferred, so a long program returns before a client's timeout and resume_research_run continues it. A test is never cut short and at least one runs per call. Unset: every test runs in this call. In s. Advanced.

hypotheses.description: each {statement, test, params, direction, prior_belief?}. test: discover_site_avoidance (params site, record?, null_model, shuffle_k/shuffles/seed under the shuffle null; direction less, greater or two-sided) or discover_codon_outliers (params gene as its library name, genetic_code, alt_init?, min_codons?; direction two-sided) or validate_gene_trait (params gene as its HGNC symbol, expression_test coexpression with trait_genes or tissue with tissues, categories as GWAS Catalog parent categories, alpha?; direction greater; needs no corpus) or discover_flag_rates (params flag as one of sigma70-strongest, splice-donor, splice-acceptor, homopolymer, tandem-repeat, long-repeat, inverted-repeat, record?, shuffle_k/shuffles/seed; direction greater, meaning beyond chance in the flag's own tail) or discover_tree_incongruence (params locus as its alignment file's name, permutations/seed; direction greater; the corpus is one aligned FASTA per locus) or discover_gene_tree_discordance (params gene as its alignment file's name, species_tree in Newick, replicates/sh_form/gamma_categories/seed; direction greater, meaning the gene fits another tree better; the corpus is one aligned FASTA per gene) or discover_reference_stability (params gene as its HGNC symbol, tissues?, neighbours?, pseudocount?; direction greater for more variable than its abundance peers, less for steadier, or two-sided; needs no corpus) or discover_annotation_contradictions (params annotation as a UniProt accession, or accession:start-end where the protein has several, feature signal or transmembrane, predictor for signal, decoding for transmembrane; direction less, meaning it scores below the experimentally confirmed features; needs no corpus) or discover_reference_concordance (params cq_table as the long-format Target,Sample,Group,Cq table itself, permutations/seed; direction greater, meaning the conditions rank the genes more alike than independent orders; needs no corpus) or differential_expression (params gene as its count-table ID, symbol? as papers name it for the literature query, counts and samples as the tables themselves, and design/reference/test/reduced/contrast/name/fitType/sfType/lfcThreshold/altHypothesis/cooksFilter/cooksCutoff/minReplicatesForReplace as the tool takes them; direction greater for higher in the contrast's numerator, less for lower, or two-sided; one-sided needs the Wald test at lfcThreshold 0; needs no corpus) or gene_set_overrepresentation (params set as its GMT ID, genes, geneSets as GMT text, universe?, forceUniverse?, minGSSize?, maxGSSize?; direction greater; needs no corpus) or gene_set_enrichment (params set as its GMT ID, ranked as 'gene statistic' lines, geneSets as GMT text, minGSSize/maxGSSize/exponent/scoreType/eps/sampleSize/nPermSimple/seed; direction greater for toward the top of the list, less for the bottom, or two-sided; needs no corpus). prior_belief: the proposer's belief before any result, one sample or a list of them (true, false, definitely true, maybe true, uncertain, maybe false, definitely false, cannot comment).

kappa.description: κ of the p-to-e calibrator e = κ·p^(κ−1); fixed for a ledger once it holds evidence. Advanced.

ledger.description: a ledger file from an earlier run, to continue: its hypotheses keep their evidence and new ones are added beside them.

organism.description: the organism the corpus is from, for the literature query each supported hypothesis needs. Advanced.

posterior_beliefs.description: each {id, samples}: the proposer's belief in a hypothesis after reading its evidence. With prior beliefs these give the follow-up order by Bayesian surprise.

run.description: a run file from an earlier call, to continue it: its seal and its pinned inputs are checked, hypotheses whose test failed or was deferred are retried, new ones are added, and nothing answered is run again.

sequences.description: the corpus every registered test runs over: library document or file names, or wired records.

name: run_discovery_programme

decisions.description: every hypothesis: verdict (supported, not-supported, no-evidence), product e-value and tests

followUp.description: hypotheses with prior and posterior beliefs, most surprising first: what to test next, never a verdict

ledger.description: the whole ledger as a jane.discovery-ledger file, every hypothesis and its evidence with traces

report.description: the program as text lines: registrations, runs, refusals, verdicts, literature queries

run.description: the whole program as a sealed jane.research-run file: the ledger, every corpus input pinned by SHA-256, the last attempt at each hypothesis. Pass it back to continue
